data.long_meaning: Derived from the Latin word 'flos', meaning 'flower' or 'gold'. The name Flavius was commonly given to Romans of noble or distinguished birth. In the Christian tradition, it is associated with the early Church Fathers, such as Flavius Clemens, who was a bishop of Rome and a Doctor of the Church. The name Flavius carries the meaning “Golden, yellow, or flour-like” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Flavius usually hope their child will grow to embody golden, yellow, or flour-like and live with faith, good character and purpose.
